judgments.reasoning_cat1: The term and the incorporation-by-reference formula ("the present contract with the changes made by this Memorandum") are definite as to dates and mechanism. The only softness is which document is "the present contract," but that is identified elsewhere as the 1981-84 booklet.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with paragraph 14 (survival of prior agreements subject to modification) and paragraph 15 (execution of a new consolidated document). No contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount" combined with "an additional $3.67 per shift from wages and after taxes ... shall be contributed to the Welfare Fund" leaves genuinely unclear whether the $3.67 is an employer contribution or an employee wage deduction, and what the "maximum of five (5) shifts" caps. The passive voice hides the obligor, which is the very kind of term a fund-contribution dispute turns on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against the Section 13-H.1 revisions (c038-c040), which recast the same $3.67 as an "after tax deduction from wages," and against Earnings Bonus paragraph 8 (c055), which excludes certain amounts from fund contributions; the pieces do not obviously line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare schedule of dated dollar increases to the journeyman day scale; the figures and dates are specific and leave nothing to construe beyond OCR noise. No vague or multi-meaning term appears.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a) and with the cost-of-living provision in 2(c); no other provision purports to set the day scale differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It incorporates "the relevant provisions of the Contract" without identifying them, and the bracketed index sentence (with "hall" for "shall" and the mismatched bracket/paren) is of uncertain operative status. Whether the bracketed index designation is binding or merely descriptive is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The COLA mechanics live in the unattached 1981-84 booklet, so fit cannot be fully verified, but nothing in this Memorandum contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is materially incomplete ("full force and effect at the Edison, New Jersey by The Times within the Northeast Corridor"), and a later sentence about listing protected regular situation holders is likewise broken; "every effort shall be made," "to the extent practicable" and "layoffs ... because of the introduction of automated processes" are all open-textured. Both a mechanical gap and vague standards are present.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its broad arbitration commitment covers "any dispute concerning the interpretation and application of the Contract," which fits paragraph 4's arbitration referral, but the layoff protection here overlaps uneasily with the Appendix A staffing commitments.
judgments.clause_name: 3. Application of Contract at New or Rebuilt Facilities; Arbitration

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The most-favoured-nation trigger turns on a "wage and benefit package which is additional to or different from that contained herein" and on the proviso that benefits were not "granted in exchange for productivity improvements or attrition, or ... diverted from an existing or subsequently negotiated wage and benefit package" — each phrase is contestable, and the parenthetical list of unions raises an expressio unius question. The double negative in the proviso compounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Earnings Bonus paragraph 7 (c054), which lets the Union apply $25.93 to "any fringe benefit ... negotiated by any other union," so the two adoption rights could be argued to overlap or duplicate.
judgments.clause_name: 4. Most Favored Nation Wage and Benefit Package

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional undertaking to execute "such agreements and execute such documents ... as are necessary to administer" the Welfare Fund; "as are necessary" is somewhat open but the class is bounded by the enumerated examples. The obligation and trigger are otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 5(c) expressly caps the financial reach of this subparagraph, so the two read together coherently; no other provision conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel in structure to 5(a) and equally definite as to trigger and required acts, with only the mild "as are necessary" qualifier. Nothing carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5(c) and with the Earnings Bonus paragraph 8 carve-out concerning pension fund contributions; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Beyond its obligation to make contributions required by the Contract for The Times deliverers" defines the cap by reference to another instrument, leaving the amount of that obligation to be established elsewhere. The savings language itself is clear in function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because it fixes the outer limit of contribution liability it must be harmonised with 2(a), the Section 13-H.1 revisions and Earnings Bonus paragraph 8, and in a fund-contribution dispute those provisions pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference to Appendix A with no operative content of its own. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix A exists in the document and its items match; consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated protected characteristics ("color, race, sex, religion or national origin") are a closed list with no catch-all, which invites an expressio unius argument about omitted grounds such as age. Otherwise the prohibition is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision of the Memorandum addresses discrimination; it fits the hiring-practices amendment scheme without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely administrative promise to furnish a letter identified as Appendix D. Definite and self-executing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix D is in fact attached and addresses Section 3-P as described; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: 8. Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance Increase

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Group I employees not so scheduled" has no antecedent in this paragraph — nothing earlier states what they are or are not scheduled for — so the covered class is uncertain. The averaging formula itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing antecedent presumably resides in Section 13-J of the 1981-84 agreement, which is not before us; nothing in this Memorandum contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Whenever the Publisher has one or more Plants, there shall be a foreman or assistant foreman in each plant" is definite in requirement but the disjunctive "or" leaves the choice and staffing level arguable. The "one or more" opener is redundant rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the new/rebuilt-facility provisions in paragraph 3 (Edison, Carlstadt) without contradiction, though it fixes a supervisory requirement at every such plant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An administrative promise to deliver a letter attached as Appendix C; no operative standard requiring construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix C is attached and sets weekly welfare contributions; consistent with this reference.
judgments.clause_name: 11. Letter Regarding Weekly Welfare Fund Contributions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical administrative form to paragraph 11, referencing Appendix D. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix D matches the description; no inconsistency with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to execute a letter about "Status Quo" and Merits arbitrator designations; the labels are undefined here but the operative act is definite. Low ambiguity on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix E, the attached letter, only says the parties will meet within sixty days to "effectuate the designation process," which is thinner than the promised letter of understanding — a mild gap.
judgments.clause_name: 13. Letter of Understanding on Arbitrator Designations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It sweeps in "all letter agreements, side agreements, supplementary agreements, memoranda of agreement and memoranda of understanding" plus the 1981-84 booklet, then declares this Memorandum prevails over "any other agreement" — the reach of the survival clause and of "conflict" is contestable, and "all dates ... shall be updated" is vague. A general catch-all sits over enumerated categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the contract's own conflict-resolution rule, so it is the provision a court would use to sort out the tensions between 2(a), the Section 13-H.1 revisions and the Earnings Bonus letter, and its interaction with the side letters (e.g. c059 preserving parts of the 1983 West Side agreement) is not free of doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Promptly" is soft but the obligation — prepare and execute a consolidated document embodying the agreed changes — is clear. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's incorporation approach and paragraph 14's survival rule; the Memorandum remains operative pending the new document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence effectiveness clause keyed to Union ratification; unambiguous. The date of ratification is a fact, not a construction question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several provisions run from "ratification" (paragraphs 8, 9, Appendix C), all consistent with this trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition "[s]ubject to there being no increase in the number of floor hires as set forth in the Collective Bargaining Agreement" is a cross-referenced cap whose content and effect on the promised ten situations is not stated. Whether the condition is precedent or merely descriptive is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside 1.B and paragraph 3's layoff protections without direct contradiction, though the floor-hire cap and added situations could be said to pull against each other.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix A, 1.A. Ten Additional Floor Regular Situations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical schedules ("Wednesday-Saturday night ... and Sunday night") and "five additional chauffeurs on dayside (4 days and Monday night)" are internally odd — dayside plus a night — which invites argument about the shifts created. The numbers themselves are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It shares the same "subject to no increase in floor hires" opener as 1.A and is otherwise consistent with Appendix A as a whole.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix A, 1.B. Five Additional Floor Regular Situations and Chauffeurs

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence creating a single regular situation for the third recovery car; concrete and complete. Nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses recovery cars; consistent with Appendix A.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix A, 2. Third Recovery Car Situation

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ministerial updating of names on identified booklet pages; definite in scope. No contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Four Man Board award later revises the same Paragraph 3 at pp. 103-5, so the two updating instruments touch the same text, but they address different sentences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall continue to be served by" preserves an unstated existing practice, and "delivery points designated by the Publisher" gives unilateral discretion with no standard; "T-Route contractors" is undefined. Both features leave room for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the West Side Direct and Honor Box provisions in Appendix B and the "present practices" side letter, which together define delivery methods by reference to practice rather than text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Times shall have the right to reorganize these routes" is qualified only by a proviso that "the present number of routes ... shall not be reduced," leaving "reorganize" and "present number" to be fought over. The tension between an abolition of the prior agreement and a preserved route count is on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The September 9, 1988 letter (c059) says the "abolition" does not affect any other agreement regarding those routes except the attrition portion, which qualifies this sentence and is not easy to reconcile with an outright abolition.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix B, West Side Direct Routes

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A garbled one-line cross-reference ("se. Appendix B-1") but its sense — see Appendix B-1 — is recoverable. Little operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix B-1 exists and addresses Honor Boxes and Vending Machines, and the outside counsel letter supplies the practice memorandum; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix B, Honor Boxes and Vending Machines

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except unsold current copies on 'bulldog' routes" carves out an undefined category, and "the headsheet or other designated portion" plus "[a]ny existing physical pick-up ... shall continue" both depend on unstated existing practice. The exception-to-a-general-rule structure is a live scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Saturday Night Bulldog guarantee and the home-delivery provision in the same appendix without direct contradiction, though all three rest on "existing practice."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole obligation is to "maintain present Practices," a phrase with no content on the face of the letter and the classic vague term. Whose practices and as of when are unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Spinelli memorandum (c058) is supplied precisely because "present practices" needed defining, and counsel's covering letter says those are the practices continued — an external gloss that may or may not be operative under paragraph 14.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix B-1, Honor Boxes and Vending Machines Side Letter

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Contributions to the Welfare Fund ... shall be made weekly" and "made available no later than ten (10) days following the end of such payroll week" are definite as to timing but silent on the base and rate of contribution. "Made available" rather than "paid" is a small but real ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 2(a) and the Section 13-H.1 revisions to know what is being contributed weekly, and this contribution machinery is exactly where the Earnings Bonus paragraph 8 carve-out bites.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix C, Weekly Contributions to the Welfare Fund

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter itself concedes the terms "Grandfather" and "Grandmother" "have not always been interpreted and applied consistently," and its cure — the grandparent "of a Regular Situation Holder or Group I Extra or of his or her spouse at the time the grandparent dies" — still leaves step- and in-law relationships open. An acknowledged inconsistency is textual evidence of ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to state one party's "interpretation" of Section 3-P, which is not reproduced here, so a divergence between letter and section cannot be excluded; paragraph 12 makes the letter part of the deal.
judgments.clause_name: Appendix D, Section 3-P Interpretation of Grandfather/Grandmother

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear temporal limitation: no retroactive effect and no use in support of claims for deaths before the letter's date. The operative cut-off is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the natural companion to the preceding clarification and does not conflict with paragraph 12 or paragraph 14's survival rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quoted replacement sentence is mangled and incomplete ("may elect to accumulate a ll ef hi ... leave days"), and the deletion instruction breaks off mid-sentence, so the resulting text of Section 13-K.2 cannot be reconstructed with confidence. That is a mechanical defect that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Removing the liquidation-on-expiration sentence while paragraph 1 fixes a six-year term raises a question about what happens to accumulated leave at the end of the term, which no other provision answers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ertain neutrals" are identified nowhere in the letter, and the commitment is only to "meet ... to effectuate the designation process" — an agreement to agree with no fallback. The soft obligation is the ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 13 promised a "letter of understanding regarding the designations of 'Status Quo' and Merits Arbitrators," and this letter does not address that distinction, leaving a gap between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Times shall negotiate the conditions" is a bare duty to bargain with no substantive outcome, and "when the normal daily order reaches 2500 copies" leaves "normal" and the measurement period undefined. Both the trigger and the obligation are indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the pattern of other negotiate-later commitments (Glen Burnie/Lancaster, Edison magazine transport) and does not contradict any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]atisfactory arrangements," "the revised Glen Burnie agreement," and "shall not involve The Times in increased costs" are each open-ended, and the assignment obligation is conditioned on a chain of undefined events. Whose satisfaction and which costs count are unresolved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The following paragraph makes a parallel Edison commitment on the same "no increased costs" condition, so the two are consistent in approach even if both are soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Performance is conditioned on the parties having "resolved satisfactorily any grievances, differences and disputes" and the plant "running," then only to "negotiate ... arrangements" subject to no increased cost — a stack of vague conditions on a duty to bargain. Nothing is definitely promised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the Edison staffing disputes contemplated in paragraph 3, and the two are consistent, though paragraph 3 channels such disputes into arbitration while this leaves them to negotiation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise numeric substitution of "7.678%" for "6-1/2%" said to "reflect the present welfare contribution percentage"; the figure is definite though the base to which it applies lives in Section 13-H.1. Little internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The percentage's base interacts with 2(a)'s statement that pension and welfare contributions are made on the increased scale and with the Earnings Bonus paragraph 8 exclusion, so the contribution base is a point of potential friction.
judgments.clause_name: Revision of Section 13-H.1(a) Welfare Contribution Percentage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instruction is to add "and an after tax deduction from wages of $3.67 after the words 'per shift'" with an unclosed quotation, so the resulting sentence — and whether the $3.67 is a contribution obligation or a payroll deduction — cannot be read off the text. That is a mechanical defect bearing directly on meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It recasts the same $3.67 that 2(a) describes as "from wages and after taxes ... contributed to the Welfare Fund," and the two characterisations (employer contribution vs employee deduction) are not obviously reconcilable.
judgments.clause_name: Revision of Section 13-H.1(b) After Tax Deduction

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 1987 figure is garbled ("§.00 per shift"), so the first amount in an otherwise ascending schedule of casual contributions is unascertainable from the text. The remaining figures are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The schedule dovetails with 2(a)'s per-shift welfare contribution and the 13-H.1 percentage change, but the relationship between casual per-shift amounts and the $3.67 deduction is left unstated.
judgments.clause_name: Revision of Section 13-H.1(c) Casual Welfare Contributions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A targeted textual insertion — "in writing, at least sixty (60) days prior thereto" after "notify the Union" — with "[balance as in original]"; definite as an amendment instruction. The underlying Section 9B is not reproduced, but the inserted words are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The immediately following paragraph qualifies the same sixty-day notice, and the two read together coherently as rule and exception.
judgments.clause_name: Amend Section 9B - Sixty Day Notice Insertion

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] New York Times part or section regularly inserted" and "the promptest practicable notice" are both vague, and the excuse turns on The Times being able to "demonstrate that it did not have sixty (60) days' notice itself" — an evidentiary standard left undefined. The final sentence's saving of "any other notice requirements" adds scope uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly does not "modify any other notice requirements pursuant to the Contract," which harmonises it with the rest, so no conflict is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] uniform portion of each employee's wage increase to become effective then or thereafter" is imprecise as to which increases may be tapped and how uniformity is measured, and the Union's power to divert is unbounded in amount. "Vacation pay benefit" is also undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Diverting wage increases interacts with 2(b)'s fixed scale increases and with 2(a)'s statement that pension and welfare contributions are made on the increased amount, so a diversion could reduce the contribution base without any provision saying so.
judgments.clause_name: Diversion of Wages to Vacation Pay Benefit

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ominal administrative costs" and a duty to "fully cooperate" in developing "any such alternatives" are standards without measurable boundaries. The no-increased-cost condition is the operative constraint and is itself elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the preceding diversion right and matches the same no-increased-cost formula used in the Glen Burnie/Lancaster letters; no conflict found.
judgments.clause_name: No Increased Cost from Diversion; Cooperation

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A commitment only to establish a four-person committee "to study possible methods," with no substantive obligation; the softness is total but there is little to construe because nothing is promised. "Terminally ill" is undefined but no entitlement turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Memorandum addresses assistance to ill employees; it stands alone consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative object of the guarantee is missing from the text ("it will guarantee all Saturday night Bulldog uding routes and relays)"), so what is guaranteed — situations, shifts, work — cannot be determined. That is a mechanical gap going to the heart of the promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relates to the bulldog-route carve-out in the returns provision (c028) and to Appendix A staffing, but with the guarantee's object missing no conflict can be pinned down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment is specific as to rate, year and waiver of recalculation, though "notwithstanding any provision to the contrary" is an unlocated override and the exception for 1987 retroactive wages paid in 1988 is intricate. The intricacy is precise rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same 1987-retroactivity exclusion is repeated in the gross wages definition (4(a)), so the two are aligned; the "notwithstanding" phrase potentially displaces other provisions but none is identified as contrary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single percentage applied to gross wages for named calendar years; the only undefined term, "gross wages," is expressly defined in paragraph 4(a). Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of the Earnings Bonus letter as a coherent scheme; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stub-period application of the same 3.86% rate with fixed start and end dates; unambiguous. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 6's provision for payment of the stub-period bonus and with the contract term ending March 30, 1993.
judgments.clause_name: Earnings Bonus 3. Bonus for January 1 - March 30, 1993

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Gross wages" is tied to a specific W-2 line item with two stated exclusions, which is about as concrete as such a definition gets. The 1988 carve-out is detailed but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by 4(b) for disability and workers' compensation shifts and used consistently by paragraphs 2, 3 and 7; no incoherence found.
judgments.clause_name: Earnings Bonus 4(a). Definition of Gross Wages

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The add-back is confined to shifts covered by The Times Disability Plan and applies only "to the extent" the benefits do not appear on the W-2, which is a definite mechanism. "State disability benefit or workers' compensation benefit" is standard terminology.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 4(a)'s W-2 base and with paragraph 8's separate treatment of workers' compensation wage-rate reporting; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Earnings Bonus 4(b). Disability and Workers' Compensation Benefits

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat sixty-day payment deadline tied to the end of the applicable bonus period. No contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraphs 6 and 7 set different deadlines (thirty and sixty days) for termination and stub-period scenarios, which are exceptions to rather than contradictions of this rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause fixes a default on failure to agree — the bonus ceases and "$25.93 at the Union's option shall be added to the weekly wage scales or allocated in the manner set forth in Paragraph 7" — but whether the Union's option is over the amount, the allocation, or both is unclear, and "in accord with the Contract" is unspecified. The interplay of cessation, option and payment of the stub period invites competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to paragraph 7, which grants an overlapping in-term termination right with its own $25.93 allocation, and paragraph 8 assumes the bonus "applies" for wage-rate purposes — the three must be harmonised carefully.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Union may apply $25.93 "to the weekly wage scales or to any fringe benefit provided under the contract or negotiated by any other union and the Times in connection with the current extension negotiations or at any time through March 3[0], 1993" — the temporal and substantive reach of that string is genuinely unclear, and the date is mistyped. The general "any fringe benefit" sits against a specific negotiation context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the most-favoured-nation right in paragraph 4 and with Earnings Bonus paragraph 6's post-term default, and paragraph 8's exclusion of fund contributions on the notional $25.93 sits uneasily with adding it to the wage scales.
judgments.clause_name: Earnings Bonus 7. Union's Right to Terminate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny benefit ... which is calculated on or determined by the employee's wage rate" is a broad catch-all followed by non-exhaustive examples ("by example, but not limitation") and then a specific exclusion for Welfare and Pension Fund contributions, which is the classic general-versus-specific scope problem. "[S]o as to eliminate any duplication" adds further indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence's denial of fund contributions on the notional $25.93 stands against 2(a) ("[p]ension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount") and the percentage-of-wages formula in the Section 13-H.1 revision, which is precisely the kind of internal tension a welfare-fund contribution dispute exploits.
judgments.clause_name: Earnings Bonus 8. Benefit Calculation as if Wages Increased

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The number in the first sentence of Paragraph 3 is now eighty-eight (88)" identifies neither what the number counts nor the sentence's content, so the provision is unintelligible without the 1981-84 booklet page. Amendment by description rather than restatement is a real defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It revises the same Paragraph 3 at pp. 103-5 that Appendix A item 3 also updates, so two instruments touch the same text and their combined effect must be pieced together.
judgments.clause_name: Four Man Board Award 1. Number in First Sentence of Paragraph 3

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deletes "[t]he sentence providing for certain floormen being available for driving assignments" without quoting it, so which sentence is removed depends on identification rather than text. "Certain floormen" compounds the imprecision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Removing floormen's driving availability interacts with Appendix A's creation of additional chauffeur and floor situations, though no direct contradiction is apparent.
judgments.clause_name: Four Man Board Award 2. Deletion of Floormen Driving Sentence

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The memorandum describes practice in scrambled form (locations run together, one address incomplete) and adds an open-ended statement that as machine numbers increase deliveries are folded "into one of the three locations," so the future rule is indeterminate. The parenthetical count "(now 121)" fixes a moving figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is offered as the content of "present practices" preserved by the Appendix B-1 side letter, but it is an internal memorandum transmitted by counsel rather than an executed term, so its status under paragraph 14 is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence layers negatives — the "abolition" "shall not affect any other agreement contained therein or otherwise regarding those routes other than that portion providing for attrition" — so what survives the abolition and what "or otherwise" reaches are both genuinely uncertain. "[T]hat portion providing for attrition" is not quoted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix B says the 1983 West Side Direct memorandum "shall be abolished" outright and gives The Times a right to reorganise, which this letter substantially qualifies; that is a direct tension between two operative documents in the same package.
